english.title: Elicit info re HM forces / intelligence service / police to assist in commission terrorism
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), elicited or attempted to elicit information about an individual who was or had been a

(A)_[member of His Majesty's forces]_
(B)_[member of any of the intelligence services]_
(C)_[constable,]_

which was of a kind likely to be useful to a person committing or preparing an act of terrorism
english.legislation: Contrary to section 58A(1)(a) and (3) of the Terrorism Act 2000.

Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure

english.notes:
(i) Section 58A(2) of the Terrorism Act 2000 provides that it is a defence for a person charged with an offence under this section to prove that they had a reasonable excuse for their action.
(ii) Section 76(2) of the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008 provides that the application of section 58A in England and Wales in relation to an offence committed before the commencement of section 154(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 the reference to 12 months is to be read as a reference to 6 months..
(iii) The penalty on indictment was increased to include a maximum of 15 years imprisonment prior to 12 April 2019; for offences prior to that date, please see document H6742.
(iv) Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the offences to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.

welsh.welshoffencetitle: Cael gwybodaeth am aelod o luoedd arfog EM/gwasanaeth cudd-wybodaeth/yr heddlu i gynorthwyo i gyflawni/paratoi

(A)_[aelod o luoedd Ei Mawrhydi]_
(B)_[aelod o unrhyw un o'r gwasanaethau cudd-wybodaeth]_
(C)_[gwnstabl,]_

welsh.welshlegislation: Yn groes i Adran 58A(1)(a) a (3) Deddf Terfysgaeth 2000.

other.penalty:
Either way -

Summary: maximum 12 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 15 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

Notes
(i) Before the commencement of section 154(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 the reference to 12 months is to be read as a reference to 6 months.
(ii) On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
